source.title: Monosemanticity in Recommender Systems
source.authors: Yagel Alfasi; Eden Rzezak; Eadan Schechter

page_placements.theme: Nested-prefix (Matryoshka-type) objectives order latents by granularity

record.tranche_reason: The study uses an MSAE as an interpretability tool and relies on the premise that Matryoshka training mitigates SAE splitting and absorption, but it does not measure feature splitting or absorption.
record.gate_note: The study reports a qualitative broad-to-specific semantic gradient across MSAE neuron indices, recorded below as a related finding. It does not compare a coarse feature with candidate child features, test whether child activations partition parent inputs, or compare feature directions across dictionary sizes. The SAE–MSAE ranking comparison and gender-neuron interventions concern recommendation behavior, not the claimed feature-splitting pattern.
record.test_reason: The study applies a Matryoshka SAE (50 latents) to matrix-factorization item embeddings, premised on Matryoshka training mitigating splitting and absorption. It never measures splitting, absorption or cross-size feature relations. There is no dictionary-size sweep and no parent/child coverage or direction comparison. The SAE-vs-MSAE comparison reports only recommendation metrics. The broad-to-specific label gradient is a product of the MSAE's own nested objective and the labeling prompt, not a test of any version.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that MSAEs expose recoverable hierarchical semantic structure in MF recommender embeddings. They also conclude that gender-associated neurons causally shift recommendation composition while keeping >0.96 overlap. Matryoshka's mitigation of splitting and absorption is asserted from prior work, not tested here.
record.recipe_differences: Applies a Matryoshka SAE to matrix-factorization item embeddings in a recommender system; it does not reproduce a feature-splitting measurement or compare feature families across dictionary sizes.

fits_no_version.finding: MSAE LLM-generated labels run from broad (neurons 0–21) to mildly demographic (22–35) to more differentiated (36–49). Monosemanticity scores are higher among later indices (top N41 0.201) and lowest among early ones (N3 0.076).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In an MSAE on Amazon Fashion MF embeddings, latent specificity increases with prefix index.

record.problems: For the related semantic-gradient finding, the study uses one dataset/domain and a latent dimension of 50; labels are generated by an LLM without reported human validation. The study itself notes that generalization to other domains and substantially larger dictionaries remains open.
record.rows_left_out: No results on feature splitting, absorption, or cross-size feature relationships were reported, so none were recorded as rows. Recommendation-ranking comparisons and gender-neuron intervention results do not measure the claim's feature-splitting behavior.

untested.parts: No dictionary-size sweep. No test of coarse features being replaced by finer features that cover their inputs and lie near their direction.
No large-model or open-SAE-release test. The setting is a 20-dim MF recommender.
No measurement of nested, geometrically close feature families. Index-ordered LLM labels are not tested against a concept hierarchy or decoder geometry.
No measurement of parent latents failing to fire where child latents take over. No test of SAE size or sparsity changes.
No decomposition of larger-SAE latents into smaller-SAE latents. No test for novel latents across sizes.
Matryoshka's reduction of splitting is assumed from the cited Bussmann et al. paper, not measured. The plain-SAE baseline is compared only on recommendation metrics.

record.verdict_notes: Three caveats apply to the R1 gradient. First, the labeling prompt forces a refined subtype when a broad label repeats earlier labels, which by itself pushes later-labeled neurons toward specificity. Second, the text says the gender axis appears exclusively among higher-indexed neurons, yet the set includes N3, an early-index neuron. Third, the ordering is designed in by the nested objective, so it cannot bear on V6 without a comparable plain-SAE analysis, which the study does not report.

versions.untested_parts: No increasing dictionary-size sweep or measurement of coarse features being replaced by finer features that cover the same inputs and lie near the coarse feature's direction.
No large-model or open-SAE-release feature-splitting test.
The reported broad-to-specific labels do not test whether split features form nested families with geometrically close directions that mirror a concept hierarchy.
No test of parent-latent firing where a child takes over, or of whether changing SAE size or sparsity fixes that behavior.
No decomposition comparison between larger- and smaller-SAE latents and no test for novel latents across dictionary sizes.
No test of whether splitting is an artifact of the sparsity objective on correlated or hierarchical inputs, or whether Matryoshka training changes splitting.

rows.subject: Matryoshka Sparse Autoencoder (MSAE)
rows.operation_detail: Qualitative analysis of LLM-generated labels across latent neuron indices
rows.measure: Semantic specificity of neuron labels by index range
rows.value: Neurons 0–21 receive broad labels; neurons 22–35 show mild demographic focus; neurons 36–49 have more differentiated labels, including specific women’s apparel subcategories, footwear types, and accessory segments.
rows.note: This is a reported semantic gradient in MSAE neurons, not a measurement of feature splitting, parent–child input coverage, or geometric proximity between split features.

relation.reason: It cites Matryoshka's mitigation of splitting and absorption from prior work as its premise and does not test it. Section 7 says this remains an open question at larger scale.

tranche.reason: The study applies a 50-latent Matryoshka SAE to MF item embeddings as an interpretability tool. It runs no dictionary-size sweep and never measures splitting, absorption, or parent/child coverage or geometry.

source_check.notes: This is not a feature-splitting test: one dataset (Amazon Fashion), one 50-latent MSAE, and LLM labels from Claude Opus 4.5 with no counts. The paper contradicts itself on N3: 5.2.2 calls N3 'higher-indexed' and says the gender axis is 'exclusively among higher-indexed neurons', but N3 has index 3.

statements.correction: Matches the text. Label bands are 0-21 (broad), 22-35 (mild demographic focus) and 36-49 (most differentiated) (5.2.2). Top MS is N41 at 0.201. Lowest are N3 0.076, N1 0.077 and N0 0.079 (5.2.1). The text says the stated range is approximately 0.075-0.201.
